evidence: The new RunE prints quickstart text with no output-mode check, so bare 'lit --json' emits prose; but the packet does not show that 'lit quickstart' rejects JSON or that any caller runs bare 'lit --json' for machine output. The reply 'stupid' gives no reasoning to check.
guidance_note: When a pushback is warranted, state the reason on the thread (e.g. 'bare lit is a human entry point, --json is meaningless without a subcommand') so the decision can be audited.

evidence: The diff hunk shows both 'if wsErr != nil { return cmd.Help() }' and 'if guidanceErr != nil { return cmd.Help() }', swallowing template-render and getcwd errors; df735f3 narrowed the fallback to workspace.ErrNotGitRepo. The defect is a silent failure, not data-vs-control-flow; an errors.Is branch is still control flow.
guidance_note: When writing a fallback, enumerate the one expected error it covers (here ErrNotGitRepo) and let every other error propagate, instead of falling back on any non-nil error.

evidence: The PR changed root-command behavior with no test of the new path in the diff; the thread is outdated and resolved without a reply, and the packet does not show whether df735f3 added the requested tests.
guidance_note: When changing a command's default behavior, add a test for each branch of the new dispatch (in-repo, outside-repo) in the same PR.

narrative: Single review round on a small change making bare 'lit' print quickstart. The real bug was the blanket error swallow (F2), fixed correctly by narrowing to the ErrNotGitRepo sentinel. F1 was dismissed with one word and F3 (tests) got no reply, so the packet cannot show whether tests were added.
guidance_observations: Two of three threads were closed with a one-word reply or none, leaving no auditable reason for the decision.
The F2 fix cited dataflow-not-control-flow for what is a no-silent-failure fix, so the law citation was attached after the fact rather than diagnosing the problem.

evidence: TestTryAcquireFileLockFailsIfExists acquires sequentially in one goroutine, so a check-then-create implementation passes it despite the 'verifies atomicity' doc comment; b2ea26a replaced it with a 32-goroutine barrier race asserting exactly one winner.
guidance_note: Before naming a test after a property (atomicity, concurrency), check that a broken implementation lacking the property would fail it.

evidence: The post-condition shown only calls GetIssue for readability, never checking comment bodies, priorities, or transition status, so dropped writes would pass; b2ea26a records per-batch plans and verifies each against persisted state.
guidance_note: In a mixed-mutation test, assert the effect of every mutation batch, not only that the rows are still readable.

evidence: The reviewer cites TestAcquireCommitLockReclaimsDeadOwner at commit_lock_test.go:93-120 asserting the same dead-PID reclamation; the agent confirmed and deleted the duplicate.
guidance_note: Before adding tests for an existing subsystem, grep its existing _test.go files for the behavior and extend rather than duplicate.

evidence: TestStaleLockFromAgeIsReclaimed (garbage content, old mtime, removeStaleCommitLock) duplicates TestRemoveStaleCommitLockRemovesStaleMalformedOwner per the reviewer's cited lines; the agent deleted it.
guidance_note: Before adding tests for an existing subsystem, grep its existing _test.go files for the behavior and extend rather than duplicate.

evidence: The doc comment of TestCommitWorkingSetRetryAfterTxCommit describes a re-entrant lock path, not a retry, so 'Retry' in the name was wrong; the agent renamed it to TestWithMutationCommitWorkingSetReentrantPath.
guidance_note: Name a test after the path its body actually drives, checked against its own doc comment.

narrative: Test-only PR; all five findings were correct critiques of test strength or duplication, and the agent accepted each with a concrete fix in one commit. No follow-up round was needed.
guidance_observations: Two of five findings were duplicates of existing commit_lock_test.go tests, so a grep of the package's existing tests before writing would have removed a third of the review.

evidence: The original migration only reset priority>1, leaving legacy 0/1 rows unchanged, which matched neither semantic; but per F9's reply the ticket said verbatim 'Reset all existing ticket priorities to normal', so the agent's remap of legacy {0,1} to urgent contradicted the spec and was reverted in 7567936.
guidance_note: Before accepting a reviewer's proposed data-migration semantics, check them against the ticket's stated migration rule and implement the ticket's rule.

evidence: The comment claimed derivation from model.PriorityNormal/PriorityUrgent while the SQL hard-coded 0/1; 5d7bc18 built canonicalPriorityCheckClause from the constants. The 7567936 diff shows that fix was later deleted, which F13 re-raised.
guidance_note: Do not write a comment claiming derivation from a constant unless the code derives from it; grep the diff for the literal values the constant replaces.

evidence: The column change is a real breaking output change, but renaming priorities is the PR's feature; the agent kept names and took the reviewer's own alternative, documenting it under a Breaking changes section of the PR description.
guidance_note: When a PR deliberately changes user-visible output, list it under Breaking changes in the original PR description.

evidence: runUpdate's 'fs.Int("priority", 0, ...)' predates review and 8f84eea only touched test fixtures; but F2's fix replaced 0/1 literals with model constants in schema.go only and did not sweep the identical literal default in cli.go, which round 1 then flagged alone.
guidance_note: When fixing a hard-coded-literal finding, grep the whole diff for every occurrence of the literal in that role and convert them in the same commit.

evidence: F1's fix (5d7bc18) detected legacy data by 'any priority outside [0,1]', which misses legacy tables holding only 0/1 values; the eed080f anchor only changed runUpdate. 7567936 keyed the migration on CHECK-constraint shape as the reviewer suggested, while also reverting to a flat reset.
guidance_note: Key a one-shot migration on a schema marker (constraint shape or version), never on whether the data happens to look legacy.

evidence: The CHECK tightening to <=1 is in the original PR and ReplaceFromExport inserted issue.Priority directly, so old exports with priority=2 would fail; eed080f only changed the runUpdate default, so the flag is a false positive. 4863bc0 added clampPriorityToCanonical at the restore boundary per the owner's direction.
guidance_note: When tightening a DB constraint, trace every insert path (create, import, restore) and decide how each handles values the new constraint rejects.

evidence: --priority-min/max accepted any integer against a 2-value domain; the help-text edit is in the original PR, not eed080f. The owner directed removing the flags and query terms rather than validating them, done in 4863bc0.
guidance_note: When collapsing a value domain, list every surface that exposes the old range (flags, query terms, filter fields) and remove or re-shape each in the original PR.

evidence: Same unvalidated range flags on lit ready, introduced in the original PR; eed080f did not touch them. Removed with readyFilter fields in 4863bc0 per the owner.
guidance_note: When collapsing a value domain, list every surface that exposes the old range (flags, query terms, filter fields) and remove or re-shape each in the original PR.

evidence: The flat reset matches the ticket text quoted in the reply; the real mismatch was that the PR description still advertised F1's remap after 7567936 reverted it. The agent updated the description and kept the code.
guidance_note: When reverting a fix, update every artifact the fix touched, including the PR description, in the same push.

evidence: This re-raises F7 because its fix was still pending when round 3 ran at 11:55 (fix landed 12:14 in 4863bc0); 7567936 only touched schema.go, so the flag is a false positive.
This re-raises F6, whose fix was still pending at round 3; the CHECK <=1 line it anchors on is original-PR code, not 7567936's change. Fixed by the same clamp in 4863bc0.
This re-raises F8, whose removal had not yet been pushed when round 3 ran; 7567936 did not touch cli.go. Removed in 4863bc0.

The 7567936 diff (the commit named as F5's fix) deletes canonicalPriorityCheckClause and restores 'CHECK(priority >= 0 AND priority <= 1)' plus 'UPDATE issues SET priority = 0' literals, undoing F2's fix; 4863bc0 reintroduced priorityCheckClause from the model constants.
guidance_note: When reverting a fix commit, diff the revert against every other review fix that commit carried and re-apply the ones that still stand.

evidence: Seeding a one-time rank backfill by legacy 'priority ASC' (lower = more important) keeps the user's old importance order in rank, which the flat priority reset does not contradict. The ensureIssueRanks-then-priority ordering in migrate dates from the original PR (hunk +171), not 4863bc0, so the flag is a false positive. The owner's bare 'no' gives no reason.

4863bc0, the fix for F7/F8, removed --priority-min/max and priority query terms while the Breaking changes section created for F3 did not list them. The thread has no reply and the packet does not show the final PR body.
guidance_note: When a fix removes a user-facing surface on a PR with a Breaking changes section, add the removal to that section in the same push.

narrative: The costliest move was accepting F1's legacy-remap semantics without checking the ticket, which said to reset all priorities to normal. That produced a data-shape detector (F5), a revert that also wiped F2's constant-derivation fix (F13), and a stale PR description (F9). Round 1 existed only because F2's fix did not sweep the identical literal in runUpdate (F4). Rounds 2-4 also carried original-PR gaps (restore path, range flags) and re-raises of fixes not yet pushed, so they would have happened anyway; 1 avoidable round is a floor.
guidance_observations: Reverting a commit to undo one fix silently undid another review fix carried in the same commit; reverts need a diff against all open review fixes.
Round 3 re-raised three findings because the owner's direction had been posted but the fixes were not yet pushed; batching the push before the next review would have saved those comments.
The original PR did not enumerate every surface of the old 0..4 domain (flags, query terms, restore path, rank backfill), which fed three rounds of reviewer discovery.

evidence: The agent confirmed existing init tests all pass --skip-agents, so the new agents_source/claude_source path was untested; f7299dc adds init_test.go covering embedded, global and human output.
guidance_note: When adding a reported field to a command, add a test that runs the command path producing it, for each source value.

evidence: OverrideLayer and the new Source both encode project/global origin; f7299dc deleted OverrideLayer and its only consumer already discarded it. The rewritten ActiveOverride doc comment, saying 'Source is the single canonical enum' on a function that no longer returns it, is what #113/F1 flagged.
guidance_note: Before adding a new enum, grep the package for an existing type encoding the same concept and extend or replace it.

evidence: Only global and embedded sources were tested for the agents-section template; f7299dc adds TestQuickstartRefreshShowsProjectSourceForAgentsSection asserting '(via project)'.
guidance_note: When adding an enum-valued output, test every enum value, starting with the highest-precedence branch.

evidence: templates_test.go only exercised Load; f7299dc adds TestLoadWithSourceReportsLayer with embedded, global and project-masks-global subtests asserting the Source value.
guidance_note: When adding a new exported function, add a unit test of its own contract next to it.

evidence: Resetting priorities is the intended migration (see #108's ticket text, 'Reset all existing ticket priorities to normal'). migrations.go is not in f7299dc's diff; it came from the unrelated commit 0076fb3 per the issue comment, so the named-fix flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Do not push unrelated commits onto a PR under review; this migration framework drew four findings on a guidance PR.

evidence: The hunk hard-codes "CALL DOLT_BRANCH('%s', 'master')" while the store runs on the checked-out branch, so the safety branch can snapshot the wrong HEAD. The thread is unresolved with no reply and the PR was closed with the migration commit 'handled separately'; the packet does not show whether this carried forward. Not caused by f7299dc, which does not touch migrations.go.
guidance_note: A recovery snapshot should be taken from the branch actually in use (HEAD), not a hard-coded branch name.

evidence: runVersionedMigrations returns runVersionedMigrationsDryRun's result, which rolls back and returns nil, so Store.Open reports success on an unmigrated DB. The owner acknowledged it ('serious error') but no fix landed and the PR was closed; the packet does not show where it went. Not caused by f7299dc.
guidance_note: A dry-run mode must stop the caller from proceeding as if the real operation succeeded, by returning a distinct result or error.

evidence: migrations.go (a 322-line versioned-migration framework) sat on a PR titled for agent guidance; the closing issue comment shows the agent split the PR, moving template work to #113 and the migration commit 0076fb3 out. f7299dc does not touch migrations.go, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Keep each PR to one ticket's scope; check the branch's commit list against the PR title before pushing.

evidence: The reviewer says fresh DBs seed schema_version 1 so every new workspace runs v2 and creates a safety branch; plausible from the hunk, but the seed site is not in the packet. Unresolved with no reply, and the PR was closed. Not caused by f7299dc.
guidance_note: Seed a fresh database at the latest schema version so forward migrations only run on real upgrades.

narrative: Round 0 findings on the template-source feature were all correct and fixed well in f7299dc. Round 1 findings all target migrations.go, which arrived from an unrelated commit (0076fb3) pushed onto the branch, not from any fix. The PR was then closed and split, leaving F6, F7 and F9 unresolved on this thread with no visible carry-forward. The F2 fix left a doc comment that #113/F1 later flagged.
guidance_observations: Stacking an unrelated migration-framework commit onto a guidance PR drew five findings and forced a split; scope checks belong before push.
Closing a PR with unresolved correct findings (F6, F7, F9) and no pointer to where they went risks losing them.

evidence: The agent says printUsage has no callers and pastes cobra help listing 'prefix' from the registry, so users never see stale help. The packet cannot confirm the grep but shows the help output. The kernel, a hand-maintained command list drifting from the registry, was removed in 84b4e0e.
writeConfig used os.WriteFile, which truncates then writes, so an interrupted 'prefix set --apply' can leave config.json empty; 7bdee9d writes a same-dir temp file and renames it.
guidance_note: Any in-place rewrite of a file the program needs to start must write a temp file and rename it, decided when the write path is first added.

evidence: runPrefixSet checks len(positional) but not fs.NArg(), so 'lit prefix set newproj typo' drops 'typo'; the agent names runComment as the canonical pattern it missed and added the check plus a test in 7d30ec3.
guidance_note: When adding a command, copy the arg-validation of the existing canonical command of the same shape (here runComment's two checks) rather than writing a subset.

narrative: One round, three findings, all handled well: the agent verified F1's premise against real help output and acted on the kernel (dead printUsage), and accepted the atomic-write and extra-arg findings with tests. No fix-caused follow-ups.
guidance_observations: The agent checked F1's claim against actual cobra output before deciding, which correctly turned a wrong premise into a dead-code removal.

evidence: The new guard tests strings.TrimSpace(in.TargetStatus) != "" but passes the untrimmed value on, so two notions of empty coexist; whether whitespace-only input is reachable or DefaultOpen trims is not in the packet. No reply on the thread.
guidance_note: Normalize an input once at the top of the function and branch on the normalized value, rather than trimming only inside the condition.

narrative: Single-commit bug fix with one reviewer note about inconsistent trimming of TargetStatus. The agent did not reply, and the packet does not show whether whitespace input can reach ApplyUpdate.
guidance_observations: The only finding was resolved without a reply, so there is no record of why it was dropped.

evidence: The ActiveOverride doc comment written in #109's f7299dc (the F2 fix) says 'Source is the single canonical enum' on a function that returns no Source. The thread is outdated after ff70096 and round 1 had no comments, suggesting a silent fix, but there is no reply or diff in the packet.
guidance_note: After deleting a type, re-read every comment the fix wrote and check that each describes what the function now returns.

narrative: This PR is the template-source work split out of #109. Its only finding is a stale doc comment introduced by #109/F2's fix, and round 1 exists only to re-review the change for it. A careful re-read of the comment in #109 would have avoided the round.
guidance_observations: The thread was resolved with no reply even though the code apparently changed, leaving no link from the finding to its fix.

evidence: 'applyRequested := *applyVal != ""' treats --apply= as no flag, so guided mode prints the preview instead of refusing; 8285e06 switches to fs.Changed("apply") and adds TestRunTransitionDoneApplyEmptyValueIsRefused.
guidance_note: When a flag's presence carries meaning, detect it with Changed(), not by comparing its value to the zero value.

evidence: A window between GetIssue and TransitionIssue exists, but the PR's stated contract is forcing a preview run, which the window does not weaken. The agent explained that a store-level CAS is a separate design concern.

renderGuidance only substitutes <token> when present, so an override lacking it makes apply impossible; 8285e06 adds requireTokenPlaceholder, which refuses in guided mode and names the override path. Note the new helper discards ActiveOverride's error ('path, _, _ :='), unflagged.
guidance_note: When a feature makes a template placeholder mandatory, enforce it at template load in the original PR and audit every template that references the changed invocation.

evidence: F3 was about templates still telling agents to run bare --apply; its fix enforced <token> in pre-guidance overrides but did not sweep quickstart.md, which still said 'lit done <issue-id> --apply'. 1d1078e redirects quickstart to the pre-guidance instead of spelling the token form.
guidance_note: When a fix addresses stale invocation text in one template, grep all embedded templates and docs for the same invocation in that fix.

narrative: Round 0 raised three good points: the empty-value flag bug, a TOCTOU that was reasonably pushed back on, and templates lacking <token>. The F3 fix guarded pre-guidance overrides but did not sweep the embedded quickstart template that still taught bare --apply, which round 1 flagged as F4. A repo-wide grep for '--apply' during the F3 fix would have removed round 1.
guidance_observations: Changing a CLI invocation contract should come with a grep of every template and doc for the old invocation, in the original PR or at latest in the first fix.

evidence: migrateMarkers returns early unless oldBegin is present, so a file with only the legacy end marker keeps it and the upsert appends a second section; 2579043 triggers on either marker.
guidance_note: When writing a pair-rewrite, enumerate the partial states (begin only, end only) and make the early-out cover each.

evidence: No test seeded legacy markers in a hook file; 2579043 adds TestHooksInstallMigratesLegacyMarkers asserting rewrite, a single section and preserved user content.
guidance_note: When adding a migration path, add a test seeded with the legacy input in the same PR.

evidence: The agent confirmed TestLoadWithSourceReportsLayer still asserted 'BEGIN LINKS INTEGRATION' and was the CI failure on the branch; fixed in 2579043.
guidance_note: When renaming a string constant, grep the whole repo, tests included, for the old literal and run the suite before pushing.

evidence: The AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md write path gained migrateMarkers with no upgrade test; 2579043 adds TestEnsureLinksAgentFilesMigratesLegacyMarkers covering both files.
guidance_note: When adding a migration path, add a test seeded with the legacy input in the same PR.

narrative: Marker rename with a legacy-migration helper; all four findings were correct and fixed in one commit. One of them was a red CI test that still asserted the old marker, which pushing with a failing suite left for the reviewer to find.
guidance_observations: The PR was opened with CI red on a stale assertion; running the suite and grepping for the old literal before opening would have removed one finding.
